metadata.jobDescription:
Circle - Developer Pillar Organization

Circle is a Web3 infrastructure company building the rails for the internet of money.
Beyond USDC, Circle provides APIs, SDKs, and programmable wallets for developers
building on blockchain infrastructure.

Team responsible for:
- USDC on-chain development
- L1 ARC launch
- Developer tools and integrations

Context from initial conversation with Thomas:
- Multiple openings across the Dev pillar organization
- Approach: find right person first, then align to appropriate role
- 4-5 hires made last year, 2-3 more planned this year
- Interest in AI agent economy and real-world USDC use cases

Background alignment:
- Developer relations and integrations focus
- EVM integration experience from Anchorage
- Institutional custody and staking background
- AI research interest: agent-to-agent transactions using USDC

hero.subheadline: Technical Product Manager. From shipping one of Microsoft's first blockchain projects to Anchorage's protocol integrations—8 years making it easier to build on blockchain.

about.tagline: From dev tools to institutional custody—shipping Web3 infrastructure that builders actually use.
bio:
I started in 2017 with one of Microsoft's first blockchain projects—Xbox royalties on Ethereum. Since then: building Ankr's Advanced API serving 1M+ daily requests, improving Flow developer onboarding by 60% at Dapper, and leading the EVM integration team at Anchorage shipping 8 protocol integrations at 4× industry speed. The thread through my career is the same: make it easier for developers to build on blockchain.
I got into this space because of a real problem: sending money across Eastern Europe still runs on broken rails. When I saw crypto kiosks appearing in remote European towns, I knew stablecoins had crossed from speculation to infrastructure. Circle is building the platform that makes global value transfer as simple as an API call—{{accent}}and that's the Circle I want to help build.{{/accent}}
